question: Who competes with BSP for home-services deals?
html:
Answer: In Punctual Pros' PA/NJ footprint, BSP's most direct rivals are Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy Service Partners/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally Services (Watchtower) and Northwinds (TruArc). National consolidators such as Apex (Alpine) and Wrench (LGP) set add-on pricing across the sector (Private-equity landscape).

Local and national rivals

RivalSponsorPosition
SilaGoldman SachsKing of Prussia; 2,500+ staff; revenue est. $450–650M (low confidence)
Legacy/HL BowmanGridironScaled; borrows at S+425–475, marked at par
Ally ServicesWatchtowerBuying in Central PA/NJ
NorthwindsTruArcBuying in or next to Punctual Pros' counties
HallerNot statedLancaster; 254 trucks
Horizon ServicesLenders (ex-New Mountain)3.75% PIK, marked 92.5

Sources: Private-equity landscape; Competitor filings.

  • National price-setters include Apex/Alpine, Wrench/LGP, TurnPoint/OMERS, Redwood/Altas, Any Hour/Knox Lane and T3/Riverside (Private-equity landscape).
  • At the fund level, MidOcean ($1.5B Fund VI) covers franchise services directly. Trilantic North America, CIVC and Palladium compete in a similar equity band (Private-equity landscape).

Strong and weak bidders

  • Well funded: Wrench, Apex, Redwood and Legacy have par-marked debt and delayed-draw lines for acquisitions. These are the bidders to expect in auctions (Competitor filings).
  • Constrained: TurnPoint, Horizon, Any Hour and Len the Plumber pay part of their interest in kind and are marked at 89–94 (Competitor filings). Horizon is lender-owned and Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026. Both are more likely sellers than buyers over the next 12 months (Competitor filings, est.).
  • Sila grew almost entirely by acquisition, from about 96 staff in its 2020 PPP record. It bought a training academy in 2026 (Competitor filings; Home-services company case studies).

Where BSP is disadvantaged

  • Fund I is about $335M. That compares with Trivest VII at $950M, Bertram V at $1.5B and Gridiron V at $2.1B (Private-equity landscape). BSP cannot outbid these funds on size.
  • The case studies show that buyers pay more for portfolio companies with integrated systems, membership revenue and a technician pipeline. They also show rivals failing when brand count outran integration (Home-services company case studies).
  • The context does not include current add-on multiples. A comparable-transactions set for PA/NJ HVAC and plumbing deals would answer what rivals actually pay.

Next actions

  • Build a proprietary outreach list of sub-$3M EBITDA PA/NJ shops that large-cap sponsors skip. Lead with Authority Brands territory rights and brand conversion (Private-equity landscape).
  • Before Dec 15, 2026, map Heartland and Horizon locations that overlap Punctual Pros' counties. Prepare to bid on any assets that come up for sale.
  • Commission a comparable-transactions pull on recent regional add-on multiples to replace estimates in bid models.
  • Benchmark Punctual Pros' membership count per technician against the Champions figure of about 83 (Home-services company case studies).
